answer: A mapping market pays agents to locate each vertex of a jetty and nearby yarrow beds. Assign jobs by a lottery over tokens escrowed until the survey round ends: one token gives one ticket, with no per-account bonus. Validators check a fixed ledger snapshot and count each deposit only once. Dividing 100 tokens among aliases still buys just 100 tickets. To double its expected share of paid jobs, an attacker must lock twice the capital for the same period; extra names supply no extra weight.
